message.content: Handlers return a mode/data reply hash instead of a bare status string because the handler must convey both the outcome status (success/failure/error) and the associated response data to the caller. A bare status string alone would discard the payload the handler generates (e.g., computed results, metadata, or error details), forcing the caller to rely on side effects or global state to retrieve data. The hash structure (`{status: ..., data: ...}`) explicitly separates the result category from its content, enabling the caller to branch on the status while still having direct access to the data, and allowing the framework to uniformly process, log, or forward responses regardless of whether the handler succeeds or fails.
